text:
The text contrasts two opposing views on human nature. William Golding’s 'Lord of the Flies' presents the theme that evil is inherent within humans, as evidenced by the boys' descent into savagery. In contrast, Jean-Jacques Rousseau’s philosophy suggests that society corrupts people, implying that humanity’s natural state is one of goodness and freedom. The similarity lies in both texts addressing the fundamental nature of humanity and the forces that shape behavior. The difference lies in their conclusions: Golding argues that evil is innate, while Rousseau argues that external societal structures are the source of corruption.
